hero.eyebrow: TRACK INTELLIGENCE // BETA · SAMPLE DATA · POWERED BY PYXIS-1
hero.sub: Resomix Track Intelligence is track analysis software for one recording at a time. Through 70+ measurable audio characteristics, Resomix's PYXIS-1 engine measures a song's tempo, key, rhythm, energy, harmony, timbre, spectral behaviour and structure, and turns these traits into one readable track profile.
hero.anatomyLabel: SONIC ANATOMY · ONE RECORDING, MANY MEASUREMENTS
hero.figureAlt: Sonic anatomy instrument: a track waveform acts as the central spine of the diagram. Analysis lanes are layered around it: structure sections, an energy contour, a harmony strip, a timbre ridge and an identity row. Selecting a lens brings one lane forward while the others recede, and a plain-language interpretation of that layer appears below. Sample data.
hero.title: See how the track moves, changes and [[holds together.]]

profile.title: One track. One readable profile.
profile.lead: The first level of analysis is a concise and professional summary, unbiased by charts.
profile.miniAlt: Compact profile strip: the track's six sections as blocks with the energy contour drawn above them. Sample data.
profile.tableAlt: Key measurements with their source: measured values come directly from the audio, predicted values are classification signals with confidence
profile.interp: A steady, club-oriented track with a long central breakdown, stable tempo and its highest sustained energy in the final drop. Measured values are read directly from the audio; predicted values are classification signals, shown with confidence.

structure.title: How the track unfolds
structure.lead: BPM detection and a structural score, with the waveform, beat grid and sections on one timeline. Select a section to read its role.
structure.panelLabel: STRUCTURAL SCORE · WAVEFORM + BEAT GRID + SECTIONS
structure.figureAlt: Structural score: the full waveform with a beat grid beneath it and six labelled section blocks (intro, build, drop 01, break, drop 02 and outro) with their durations. The selected section is highlighted with its energy and loudness readout. Sample data.

energy.title: How energy moves through the track
energy.lead: One continuous energy journey, with loudness and dynamic range layered beneath it, anchored to the structure.
energy.figureAlt: Layered dynamics chart: a shaded dynamic-range band, a grey loudness contour and a white energy contour drawn over section markers. The global peak in the final drop is marked in orange. Sample data.
energy.readingInterp: Reading it: intensity climbs gradually, with no abrupt jumps; the long break releases energy before the strongest section; the final drop carries the global peak, then the outro steps down rather than cutting.
energy.body: DJs check the track's flow before building a set. Producers study how arrangements are made. Curators focus on the pacing. Catalogue teams turn libraries into searchable tags. Resomix's analysis describes the music. The decision stays in your hands.

harmony.title: Key and harmonic behaviour
harmony.lead: Musical key detection with confidence. The detected key and Camelot code sit up front with a readable chromagram strip, and the full pitch evidence and harmonic relationships one step deeper.
harmony.interp: The track stays centred on G minor throughout, with its strongest tonal movement in the break: pitch content spreads, then the final drop re-anchors the key.
harmony.tonalAlt: Harmonic field: a key-agreement line across the six sections that dips during the break, above a compact chromagram strip of the twelve pitch classes over time, where G and B-flat dominate. Sample data.
harmony.chromaAlt: Chromagram: twelve pitch-class rows across the track timeline. Cells brighten where a pitch class carries more energy; G and B-flat dominate, with wider spread during the break. Sample data.

spectral.title: The texture of the recording
spectral.lead: A visual of the sound's frequencies, from deep bass to high air, described in plain language.
spectral.terrainAlt: Spectral terrain: a spectrogram field from sub frequencies at the bottom to air at the top across the track timeline, rendered in greys with orange marking the hottest regions. A brightness contour is drawn over it, rising at the final drop. Sample data.
spectral.timbreLabel: timbre evolution · band balance over time
spectral.timbreAlt: Timbre evolution: stacked bands showing how the balance between sub, body, presence and air changes across the track, sub-weighted early, with presence and air widening at the final drop. Sample data.
spectral.mfccAlt: MFCC timbral fingerprint: thirteen coefficient cells summarising the track's texture. Sample data.
spectral.textureInterp: Texture read: dark and dense through the first half, smooth, sub-weighted and percussive. The final drop lifts brightness and opens the top end without losing weight.
spectral.body: Described as measured character — dark or bright, dense or open, smooth or percussive, stable or evolving.

identity.title: A profile, not a label
identity.lead: Automatic genre, style, mood and instrumentation tagging, shown as coordinated signals with confidence. Stronger and weaker, never absolute.
identity.vibeBody: What the analysis reads from the composition: instrument balance and phrasing, as shown in the dashboard.
identity.legendAlt: Confidence envelope legend: solid orange marks strong signals, solid grey marks supporting signals, dotted outlines mark uncertain or overlapping signals
identity.overlapInterp: Primary classification: deep house. Secondary signals suggest tech house and minimal influences. The profile keeps the overlap visible instead of forcing one answer.

confidence.title: Measured, interpreted, never presented as absolute.
confidence.lead: Classification depends on context. Styles overlap. Confidence is always shown, and every number is traceable back to how it was produced.
statements: Measured values (tempo, key, loudness, structure) are read straight from the audio: the same file always returns the same profile.
Predicted values (genre, style, mood, vibe) are signals, shown with confidence. Secondary signals stay visible.
Similar styles overlap; the profile presents the overlap instead of hiding it behind one label.
Raw charts never stand alone; each carries a plain-language interpretation.
Every result is traceable to its analysis run: engine version, date and scope.

items.q: How do I find the BPM and key of a track?
items.a: Upload the track to Resomix and open Track Intelligence. Tempo, key and Camelot code are measured directly from the audio and shown with a confidence value, alongside structure, loudness and energy.

items.q: How accurate is the key detection?
items.a: Measured values such as tempo, key and loudness are read from the recording, so the same file always returns the same result, and the key is shown with its confidence and any alternative key. Predicted values such as genre and mood are classification signals, shown with confidence, never as absolutes.

items.q: Does Resomix tag genre and mood automatically?
items.a: Yes, as predicted signals. Track Intelligence reports genre and style, mood and theme, and instrumentation such as vocal presence, each with a confidence level and with secondary signals kept visible instead of forced into one label.

items.q: Can Track Intelligence enrich catalogue metadata?
items.a: For a partner catalogue, yes. The same analysis runs across every authorised recording so structure, tempo, key, mood and genre are described in the same terms for every track, and it can flag inconsistent tagging. Resomix does not edit your metadata. It gives your team consistent evidence to work from.

link.label: why tags and metadata fall short

items.q: Can I analyse my own unreleased track?
items.a: Yes. The upload is processed privately, is not used to train PYXIS-1, and the source audio is deleted no later than 24 hours after upload or analysis.

items.q: Can I get the analysis as data?
items.a: Partners can retrieve versioned, structured JSON through the Resomix API, with rhythm, tonality, loudness, mood, structure and provenance fields. Analysis access is enabled on request.
